basis: Listed on the Rebels list with founder 'Satoshi Nakamoto' and no company link: a base-layer asset with no issuing organisation, held through the treasury vehicle Ribbit BTC Holdings, LP (ADV Section 7.B). Token rule (COLLECTION.md s1; Erik's a16z ruling 7: Bitcoin out); decisions.md D2.
Listed (Rebels list; archived Our Bets page 2022-2025 linking ethereum.org): a protocol asset with no investable issuing entity. Erik's a16z ruling 7 (2026-08-30) put Ethereum out; decisions.md D2.

Listed by the firm, but MercadoLibre has traded on Nasdaq since August 2007, five years before Ribbit's first fund (2012), so no Ribbit fund could enter it through a venture round. The record shows two non-venture ties: Meyer Malka's own board seat (Forms 3, 4 and 5 he filed personally, 2013-2020; T4, a person's filing locates the person) and the adviser's 13F holding of MELI from 2023 (a public-market position, T3). Post-listing public purchase with no venture entry: out.

Listed on the archived Our Bets page 2022-2025 (sea.com, Singapore), but Sea Limited listed on the NYSE in October 2017 and the adviser's 13F carries SEA from 2023; no source names Ribbit in a Sea private round. A position first appearing as a public-market holding is out (T3; decisions.md D4).

Listed on the archived Our Bets page from 2022 (futuholdings.com) and on the Rebels list, but Futu Holdings listed on Nasdaq in March 2019 and no filing, prospectus or press item names Ribbit in a Futu private round (the EDGAR full-text sweep of every Ribbit entity name returns no Futu document). First Ribbit sighting three years after the IPO: a public-market position, out under T3 (decisions.md D4).

Listed on the archived Our Bets page in 2022 only (tinkoff.ru, Russia), but TCS Group (Tinkoff) has been listed in London since October 2013 and no source names Ribbit in a private round. A public-market position, out under T3 (decisions.md D4).

Meyer Malka is a director on Craize Snacks' 2024 Form D (a Miami snack maker); no round, post or listing names a Ribbit fund, and the firm has never listed it. A partner's board seat alone is not a verified venture investment (Erik, 2026-09-28): a personal position (T2, T4).

Lemon, Inc. (Lemon Wallet, Wences Casares's company, sold to LifeLock in 2013) filed a $5M Form D in 2012 with Meyer Malka as director and Cynthia McAdam as an executive officer, at 364 University Ave, the firm's own address. No round announcement, post or listing names a Ribbit fund (the firm's 2012-2014 Bets pages never listed Lemon), so the seat is unverified as a fund position (Erik, 2026-09-28: board seat alone is out).

OSIX Corp (Woodside, then Redwood City; officers Cary and Staci Cole) filed in 2011 and 2012 with Meyer Malka as director; the first filing predates Ribbit's first fund (Form D 2012-Q2), and nothing ties a Ribbit fund to either round. A personal seat (T2, T4).
Zachary Rosen is an executive officer and director of Brellium (New York) on its 2024 Form D: the issuer's own officer, not a Ribbit seat. Brellium's 2025 Series A press names no Ribbit fund (T4).

Zachary Rosen co-founded Pantheon Systems; the 2010-2019 Form Ds list him as the issuer's own officer, years before he appears on Ribbit's team page (2023). A founder's own company is not a firm position (T4).
Zachary Rosen is Mission Bicycles' executive officer on its 2011 Form D (San Francisco): the issuer's own officer, a decade before his Ribbit tenure (T4).
Manav Kohli is PolyOps' executive officer and promoter on its 2020, 2021 and 2025 Form Ds: his own company, before he appears on Ribbit's team page (2026). Not a firm position (T4).

Matthew Wong is Guarnerix's executive officer and promoter (New York, with Lisa Wong) on its 2015-2019 Form Ds: a namesake or the person's own company, before Matt Wong appears on Ribbit's team page (2023) (T4).
